subject.title: Add trusted preflight policies for externally visible actions

question: Should OpenClaw introduce a host-trusted fail-closed preflight contract at the durable outbound-message boundary, with broader external-action classes deferred until that contract is proven?
rationale: The security property is genuinely absent from ordinary outbound hooks, but the trusted plugin tier, configuration model, exposed metadata, timeout behavior, audit storage, and compatibility defaults define a new security boundary that automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Message-first trusted contract
options.body: Add one generic trusted preflight seam for live and recovered outbound messages, reusing plugin approval routing and deferring other action classes.

options.title: General action framework
options.body: Design a cross-tool, publication, artifact, calendar, repository, agent-sharing, and device policy framework before implementing any enforcement.

options.title: Existing surfaces only
options.body: Keep tool approvals and ordinary outbound hooks separate and document plugin composition without promising fail-closed final-delivery enforcement.

recommendation.title: Message-first trusted contract
recommendation.body: Add one generic trusted preflight seam for live and recovered outbound messages, reusing plugin approval routing and deferring other action classes.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans project security posture, core-versus-plugin ownership, configuration policy, and compatibility guarantees.
